The latest 2019 World Airport Star Ratings are announced

By:Skytrax - 30 March,2019

Short Detail

The latest World Airport Star Ratings were announced during the World Airport Awards ceremony in London on 27th March 2019, with Certification presented to Salalah International Airport, Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport, Hamad International Airport, Platov International Airport, Delhi International Airport, Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport, Haikou Meilan International Airport and Milan Malpensa Airport.

The latest 2019 World Airport Star Ratings are announced Source:Skytrax

Salalah International Airport in Oman was confirmed as a 5-Star Regional Airport. As the primary entry point to the Indian Ocean resort on the Omani south coast, the airport’s key appeal is the excellent efficiency of passenger processes from aircraft to arrival and check-in to gate.

Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi is certified as a 4-Star Airport. As a major International and domestic facility Delhi caters well to a wide range of passenger types, across full-service, leisure and low-cost markets.

More nitrogen may help offset effect of climate change on wheat: study

By:Down To Earth Magazine - 27 March,2019

Short Detail

Scientists at IIT-Khanpur found out that wheat yields improves with the increasing levels of nitrogen application despite the eleavted C02 level

Carbon dioxide enrichment had a positive effect on various growth parameters and yield attributes of wheat. Elevated carbon dioxide tended to increase crop growth rate and the fraction of leaf biomass and leaf nitrogen, especially for the nitrogen management using chemical fertilizer. Elevated carbon dioxide led to 17 per cent increase in wheat grain yield above ambient as averaged over the nitrogen fertilized treatments. Elevated carbon dioxide also resulted in higher nitrogen use efficiency.

The researchers have published their findings in the European Journal of Agronomy. Apart from Dr.Swain, the team included Swati Hazra andPratapBhanu Singh Bhadoria from the Agricultural and Food Engineering Department of IIT Kharagpur, India.

Poverty down from 55% to 28% in a decade till 2015-16, study shows

By:The Indian Express - 27 March,2019

Short Detail

According to a new version of the global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) India have reduced the it's poverty leve from 55% to 28% in a span of 10 years, A total of 271million people have moved out from the poverty level since then.

The MPI measures acute poverty and people experiencing multiple deprivations, for example, those who are both undernourished and do not have safe drinking water, adequate sanitation and clean fuel.

In India, a total of 271 million (27.10 crore) people moved out of poverty during these ten years, it said. Source:The Indian Express

The sharp reduction happened in the UPA years (Congress -led UPA was in power from 2004-05 till 2013-14), the average GDP groth during UPA period was 7.6%.

NOTE: India still had 364 million poor in 2015-16, the largest for any country, although it is down from 635 million in 2005-06.The report, covering 105 countries, dedicates a chapter to India because of this remarkable progress. However, India still had 364 million poor in 2015-16, the largest for any country, although it is down from 635 million in 2005-06.

Health ministry notifies new rules for drugs and clinical trials

By:Scroll - 27 March,2019(IST)

Short Detail

The Union Ministry of Health and Welfare released new Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 inorder to reduce the time taken to approve a new drug, thus reducing an Indian made drug's approval period to a maximum of 30 days and that of forign drugs to a maximum of 90 days.

“In case of injury to clinical trial subject, medical management will be provided as long as required as per the opinion of the investigator or till such time it is established that the injury is not related to the clinical trial,” Drugs Controller General of India S Eswara Reddy said.
